predicate.verdict_note: Reviewed the follow-up to an earlier round that raised three findings on 7da5960570. (1) Remote orphan on a models kill: fixed for a red (models is never stopped) but not for INT/TERM, which still kills models; measured. (2) GPU contention: parity now takes the fleet GPU lock, but a lock timeout reads as a model FAIL with no reason, parity runs without choom, and no test covers the flock (a sed mutant survives the existing self-test); measured. (3) Target dirs: fixed and pinned by the guard, 9 of 9 committed mutants killed; scripts/apr_bin.sh resolves the target dir through cargo metadata so CARGO_TARGET_DIR is honoured, read not run. Also found: a genuine red recorded as STOPPED when two lanes fail in the same second. All findings are advisory.

findings.failure_scenario: If the user sends an interrupt (e.g. Ctrl-C) exactly after the background lane (`"t1_$s" &`) is spawned but before its PID is recorded into `T1_STEP` (`T1_STEP[$!]=$s`), the trap handler will not iterate over the newly spawned job's PID. Because the job runs in its own process group (`set -m`), it does not receive the script's `TERM` signal and is left running as an orphaned process.
findings.summary: Race condition on lane launch leaves unrecorded lanes orphaned on interrupt

findings.failure_scenario: When the user interrupts the autopilot (e.g. via Ctrl-C), the trap sends `TERM` to every lane's process group, including `models`. This kills the local `ssh` process. Because the ssh session lacks a PTY, the remote `bash -s` and its `model_ladder.sh` / builds continue running. A subsequent run will execute concurrently in the same `$dir`, contending for the remote GPU lock and corrupting the shared `receipt.json` and build logs.
findings.source: scripts/release/autopilot.sh lines 231-233 comment: "models is never stopped: its remote leg is an ssh with no pty, so killing the local ssh would leave the remote build and ladder running..."
findings.summary: INT/TERM trap kills models lane's local ssh, leaving the remote leg orphaned and corrupting the next run

findings.failure_scenario: The guard's interrupt test (`t-int`) asserts `child_gone "$t-int"`, which only verifies that `deep`'s child process is cleaned up. It makes no assertion about the `models` lane process under interrupt conditions. This blind spot allowed the autopilot's interrupt trap to erroneously kill the `models` leg without failing the guard, directly masking the remote-orphaning regression.
findings.source: scripts/check_release_t1_lanes_joined.sh line 112: `child_gone "$t-int"` only checks the deep lane's mock child.
findings.summary: The guard's interrupt test asserts deep's cleanup but is blind to models' behavior

findings.failure_scenario: If `apr parity` causes a global OOM event on the host, the kernel's OOM killer will target the CI containers (which have `oom_score_adj 500`) instead of the `apr parity` process (which has 0). This is exactly the catastrophic pool-death incident documented in #3712. The `check_model_parity.sh` patch copied the GPU lock from `apr_locked` but erroneously dropped `choom -n 1000`, leaving the CI pool completely vulnerable.
findings.source: scripts/model_ladder.sh lines 50-53: "serialized on the fleet lock, and choom'd to 1000 so a measurement, never the pool, is the OOM victim."
findings.summary: check_model_parity.sh takes the GPU lock but omits choom, risking CI container OOM deaths
